name: Liposarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and molecular diagnostic criteria for liposarcoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant adipocytic tumor cells with varying degrees of differentiation
Detection of characteristic genetic alterations such as MDM2 amplification
Imaging evidence of a soft tissue mass with fat density and non-fatty solid components

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignant adipocytic tumor cells plus molecular evidence of MDM2 amplification
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Subtyping by histology and molecular testing is critical for prognosis and treatment planning

laboratory: Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in some cases
imaging: MRI showing heterogeneous soft tissue mass with fatty and non-fatty components
CT scan demonstrating well-defined mass with areas of necrosis or calcification
genetic: MDM2 gene amplification detected by FISH or PCR
CDK4 amplification in well-differentiated and dedifferentiated subtypes
other: Histopathological subtyping essential for diagnosis (well-differentiated, myxoid, pleomorphic, dedifferentiated)

distinguishingFeatures: Benign fatty tumor without cellular atypia
Presence of round cell component with higher grade

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of soft tissue mass
Pain at tumor site especially at night
Neurological deficits due to nerve compression
references: WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours. 5th ed. IARC; 2020.
Fletcher CDM, Bridge JA, Hogendoorn PCW, Mertens F, editors. WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone. IARC; 2013.
